newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakh bank to issue 100 mln Eurobond by year-end.
newsitem.headline: Kazakh bank to issue 100 mln Eurobond by year-end.

text.p: Kazakhstan's biggest bank, Halyk Savings Bank, plans to raise up to $100 million through a Eurobond by year-end, a senior bank official said on Monday.

"By the end of this year we will issue dollar-denominated Eurobonds for up $100 million...The maturity may be up to three years," Bahit Jolaman, a vice chairman of the bank, told a news conference. He said U.S. investment bank Lehman Brothers had been mandated last Friday to lead manage the issue.

"Most probably, the credit rating to our bank will be given by rating agencies Standard & Poor's and Moody's," Jolaman told Reuters after the conference. He said the issue would not be burdensome for the bank. "We can actually raise more than $200 million," he said.

Jolaman said the money -- to be raised in the United States, Europe and "probably in South East Asia" -- would be lent to the Central Asian state's oil and gas and non-ferrous metals industries. He said: "I do not rule out investment in aviation, rail transport and precious metals."

State-run Halyk Savings Bank -- formerly the Kazakh branch of the Soviet Union's Sberbank -- ranks first among 97 Kazakh banks according to its size and role in the economy. It has 1,400 offices nationwide and employs 11,000 people. Net profits last year were 563 million tenge against 179 million in 1995. Assets grew to 29 billion tenge from 25 billion in 1995.

Resorce-rich Kazakhstan tapped international financial markets with a debut Eurobond last year. The $200 million issue, organised by Dutch bank ABN AMRO Hoare Govett, was snapped up by investors. It was priced to yield 9.3 percent or 3.5 percentage points above comparable U.S. Treasury notes.
